entries.claim: Scope 2 consumption factors (nuclear 391, gas CC 196, coal 474 gal/MWh)
entries.source: USGS Thermoelectric Water Use 2008-2020 (Virginia plants)
entries.note:
Computed (generation-weighted, pooled 2018-2020) from USGS plant-level data, not a verbatim quote; reproducible by re-running usgs_va_factors.py. 

MANDATORY CAVEAT ON THE NUCLEAR FIGURE (added 2026-08-03): 391 gal/MWh is a TWO-PLANT FLEET AVERAGE, not a plant intensity. North Anna alone runs 735.6-741.2 gal/MWh, stable across all 13 years 2008-2020; Surry consumes 0.00 because it is once-through saline on the tidal James. The fleet figure is 391 only because North Anna is ~53% of Virginia nuclear generation. Anyone who looks up North Anna directly and compares it to 391 will conclude the model is 2x wrong unless this is stated. It must therefore accompany the constant wherever the constant appears (METHODOLOGY 18, 45.2). 

INDEPENDENT VALIDATION (READING_LOG Part 31.3): pooling all 302 Virginia plant-years in the same USGS release gives nuclear 387.9 gal/MWh (bounds 302.6-473.2) and gas 191.5 (155.8-232.8) -- the shipped 391 and 196 land within 0.8% and 2.3% respectively, well inside the published uncertainty.

entries.claim: Nuclear is RARELY but not never the PJM short-run marginal resource: 0.39% (2022), 0.62% (2023), 1.00-1.35% (2019-21) of real-time marginal units
entries.source: Monitoring Analytics, 2023 State of the Market Report for PJM, Section 3
entries.note: CORRECTS A FALSE PREMISE. The previous entry claimed 'nuclear does not appear as a marginal resource at all', sourced to the p.125 SUMMARY sentence, which does not enumerate every fuel. Table 3-69 (p.200) lists Uranium/Steam explicitly. The MMU has recommended since 2016 that PJM 'not allow nuclear generators which do not respond to prices ... to set the LMPs in the real-time market' -- status Not adopted. Lake Anna's marginal attribution is therefore ~0.87% (2022 shares) or ~1.29% (2023 shares), NOT 0.00%. The abstract now says 'under 2%'. The 43% -> ~1% relocation is unaffected.
entries.section: Types of Marginal Resources (printed p.201; PDF p.79 of the Sec.3 extract). Table 3-69 with the full 2019-2023 fuel breakdown is on printed p.200.
entries.verbatim_quote: The proportion of marginal nuclear units increased from 0.4 percent in 2022 to 0.6 percent in 2023.

entries.claim: Marginal generation is attributed to Virginia plants only
entries.source: USGS thermoelectric file, VA slice
entries.note: PJM is a 13-state RTO; the marginal unit (especially coal) is often outside Virginia. Marginal DESTINATION basins are therefore under-determined. Does not affect York->0 (METHODOLOGY 47.4).

entries.source: not published by PJM/Monitoring Analytics at this granularity

entries.claim: Simple-cycle gas turbines consume 20 gal/MWh (no steam cycle; inlet cooling / NOx water only)
entries.source: author estimate -- NO supporting file in the corpus; simple-cycle consumption is not broken out in the USGS Virginia slice
entries.note: UNSOURCED. Carries 16.5% of the marginal mix. Literature places simple-cycle consumption near zero to a few tens of gal/MWh, so the value is plausible but not evidenced here. Sensitivity: at 0 gal/MWh the blended marginal falls 165.7 -> 162.4; at 50 it rises to 170.6 (+3%). Does NOT affect the Lake Anna zero (no nuclear term).

entries.claim: The marginal case uses marginal FUEL SHARES x AVERAGE per-fuel water intensity
entries.source: PJM SOM 2023 (fuel shares) + USGS annual plant data (intensities)
entries.note: No marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (Cambium is carbon-only; METHODOLOGY 18 constraint B1). Two consequences (METHODOLOGY 55): (a) 'short-run' was INHERITED from PJM's marginal-resource statistic, which reports which units set the real-time price -- it was never a modelling choice, which is why it went undocumented until review; (b) marginal units are less efficient than fleet average (higher heat rate -> more cooling water per MWh), so average intensities likely UNDERSTATE marginal water. Affects the MAGNITUDE (165.7 gal/MWh), not the Lake Anna zero.

entries.claim: CENTRAL monthly demand shape for on-site data-center water use: ICPRB's OBSERVED monthly factors (Jan 0.7 ... Jul 1.5, Aug 1.8 ... Dec 0.8; peak-to-trough 3.0x). Supersedes the CDD-proportional model used through 2026-08-02, which gave July 3.04x and peak-to-trough 10.1x -- roughly 70% too peaky in summer and less than half the observed winter floor.
entries.source: ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Appendix A.3, Table A.3-2
entries.section: Appendix A.3, Table A.3-2: Monthly Factors for Seasonal Variation in Data Center Water Use
entries.verbatim_quote: Seasonal variation in data center water use is determined by applying monthly factors to the annual averages, based on observed usage patterns in Loudoun and Prince William Counties
entries.note: SOURCE-INTERNAL DISAGREEMENT, disclosed rather than resolved silently: ICPRB's March 2026 two-page fact sheet says summer monthly use 'can be close to three times the average annual demand', which matches the SUPERSEDED CDD model's 3.04x. The technical appendix (this entry) caps the observed monthly factor at 1.8. We follow the appendix because it is observed data rather than a summary sentence, and because 'three times' is almost certainly summer-versus-winter (1.8/0.6 = 3.0), not summer-versus-annual-average. The separate peak-DAY claim ('as much as 10 times') is unaffected. CORROBORATION: JLARC Rpt598 p.39 -- data centers 'do not currently participate in demand response programs' because 'energy use is driven by computing activity' -- an independent reason to expect a high, near-constant baseload (back-fitted b ~ 0.70-0.76, outside the old swept range of 0.10-0.50).

entries.claim: PJM RTO-wide 2023 generation mix used as a location-based accounting convention

GEOGRAPHY WARNING: the plant->basin map in this repo is VIRGINIA-only. entries.claim: eGRID SERC Virginia/Carolina resource mix -- THE COUNTY'S OWN GHG accounting basis
entries.source: Prince William County Community Energy and Sustainability Master Plan (Oct 2023), Appendix F.2; confirmed by End Note 23
entries.note: 2021 mix: coal 13.4%, oil 0.2%, gas 38.1%, other fossil 0.2%, nuclear 38.8%, hydro 1.9%, biomass 2.3%, wind 0.4%, solar 4.7%. This is the basis the county uses to measure progress against its own Board-adopted climate goals, which is why it belongs in the convention table. entries.claim: Long-run marginal: data centers account for the entire projected increase in Virginia nuclear generation, +24 TWh/yr by 2040
entries.source: JLARC, Data Centers in Virginia (Rpt598, Dec 2024), Appendix H, Tables H-4 / H-5 / H-6
entries.note: Scenario 1 (unconstrained demand) puts VA nuclear at 56 TWh in 2040; Scenario 3 (no new data-center demand) holds it at the 32 TWh baseline, flat in every year. Difference = +24 TWh, i.e. ALL of it. Table 3-1 p.29 additionally attributes +79 to +92 TWh of IMPORTS to data centers by 2040, so roughly three-quarters of the incremental energy is generated outside Virginia entirely. MANDATORY CAVEAT: E3's new nuclear is UNSITED and assumed unavailable until 2035 -- presumably SMRs, NOT North Anna uprates. This quantifies long-run marginal NUCLEAR, not long-run marginal LAKE ANNA, and must never be presented as a Lake Anna share.

entries.claim: Virginia's share of eGRID SERC Virginia/Carolina nuclear generation = 23.24%, used to scale the county's own accounting convention
entries.source: EPA eGRID2023 (egrid2023_data_rev2.xlsx, sheet PLNT23, released June 2025)
entries.derived_from: 29,662,935 MWh Virginia nuclear / 127,621,001 MWh SRVC subregion nuclear; derivation vendored at data/egrid2023_srvc_nuclear.csv
entries.note: SRVC holds 9 nuclear plants: SC 55,622,340 MWh (43.6%) Oconee/Catawba/V C Summer/H B Robinson; NC 42,335,726 (33.2%) McGuire/Brunswick/Harris; VA 29,662,935 (23.2%) North Anna 15,828,266 + Surry 13,834,669. Required because the plant->basin map in this repo is Virginia-only: without the scaling, a SERC-wide nuclear share would be distributed across North Anna and Surry alone and INFLATE Lake Anna instead of deflating it. Scaled result 12.16%; unscaled 52.33%. INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECK on egrid_serc_vacar_mix: eGRID2023 puts SRVC nuclear at 39.9% of subregion generation against the CESMP's 38.8% (2021 vintage) -- two different years, ~1 point apart.
